avoid_supplements.name: Bitter Melon
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive hypoglycemic effects; may cause severe hypoglycemia when combined with semaglutide
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; monitor blood glucose if co-use unavoidable

avoid_supplements.name: Fenugreek
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potentiates glucose-lowering effects; increases risk of hypoglycemia
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue or obtain physician approval before semaglutide initiation

avoid_supplements.name: Chromium Picolinate (high doses >200mcg/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May enhance insulin sensitivity and lower blood glucose synergistically with semaglutide
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose supplementation; use only under medical supervision with glucose monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Alpha-Lipoic Acid
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild glucose-lowering properties; additive effect possible but unlikely at typical doses
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood glucose; inform provider of concurrent use

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium Supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Semaglutide may cause gastrointestinal symptoms that affect mineral absorption; no direct interaction
caution_supplements.action: Separate dosing by 2+ hours; ensure adequate intake monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics
caution_supplements.mechanism: May alter GI motility effects; no direct pharmacological interaction documented
caution_supplements.action: Monitor GI tolerance; adjust timing if nausea or delayed gastric emptying worsens

avoid_foods.name: High-fat meals (>50g fat per meal)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Semaglutide delays gastric emptying; high-fat foods significantly worsen nausea, vomiting, and GI distress
avoid_foods.action: Restrict dietary fat to <30g per meal; prioritize lean proteins and low-fat options

avoid_foods.name: Large portion sizes
avoid_foods.mechanism: Semaglutide reduces appetite and gastric capacity; oversized meals increase risk of vomiting and intolerance
avoid_foods.action: Consume smaller, frequent meals (4-6 per day); eat slowly and chew thoroughly

avoid_foods.name: Sugar-sweetened beverages and high-glycemic foods
avoid_foods.mechanism: While semaglutide controls blood glucose, rapid glucose spikes may worsen nausea and GI symptoms
avoid_foods.action: Eliminate sugary drinks; choose complex carbohydrates and fiber-rich foods

caution_foods.name: Spicy foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May exacerbate nausea and gastric irritation in sensitive patients; not a direct interaction
caution_foods.action: Monitor tolerance; reduce spice intake if GI symptoms increase

caution_foods.name: Caffeine and alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: Both can increase nausea and dehydration risk; alcohol may impair glucose control awareness
caution_foods.action: Limit caffeine to <200mg/day and alcohol to moderate amounts; ensure adequate hydration

caution_foods.name: High-fiber foods (sudden increase)
caution_foods.mechanism: Semaglutide already slows GI transit; abrupt fiber increase may worsen bloating and constipation
caution_foods.action: Gradually increase fiber intake over 2-4 weeks; maintain consistent hydration

monitoring_notes: Semaglutide has minimal CYP450-mediated drug interactions due to low hepatic metabolism; primary concerns are supplements/foods that potentiate glucose-lowering effects or exacerbate GI side effects (nausea, delayed gastric emptying). Monitor for hypoglycemia symptoms when combined with other antidiabetic agents or glucose-lowering supplements, and assess GI tolerance at each visit.
